messages:
maya: Uploaded Sirocco9b weights to s3://redwood-models/sirocco9b/v1/ (sharded, float16). Tokenizer artifacts are in the same folder but noticed a quirk: eos appears as a separate merge in the bpe merges. Can someone quick-verify config and kick off a smoke perf run? cc @dan @priya

---
dan: Taking a look. Can you paste the exact weights path (including manifest) and the default config you used? Also which seq_len we should target for the smoke run?

maya: Path: s3://redwood-models/sirocco9b/v1/model-00001-of-00008.pt and manifest: s3://redwood-models/sirocco9b/v1/manifest.json. Default config I pushed to repo: 
```
model:
  name: sirocco9b
  dtype: fp16
  seq_len: 2048
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
tokenizer:
  path: s3://redwood-models/sirocco9b/v1/tokenizer.json
  add_prefix_space: false
```
I put seq_len 2048 to be safe but happy to reduce if needed for latency.

infra-bot: artifact-uploaded: s3://redwood-models/sirocco9b/v1/manifest.json (uploader: maya) :package:

bench-runner: Quick note — for 9B models we usually run smoke with seq_len=1024 and test batch sizes [1,2,4]. If you keep 2048 we'll see significant latency and may time out on smaller infra tiers. Also tokenizer.add_prefix_space=false may cause prompt token offsets if our prompt templates rely on leading spaces.

priya: Thanks — observed the same eos split with a different model earlier. Suggest setting `add_prefix_space: true` in tokenizer config and regenerate the tokenizer.json symlink for serving. That fixes a bunch of off-by-one prompt tokenization issues in our evals.

ben: I have a small PR open with the config tweaks and a tokenizer patch: https://git.internal/redwood/inference-config/pulls/518 — includes seq_len=1024 for smoke and add_prefix_space=true. @maya can you attach the model manifest CID to the PR for traceability?

maya: Attached manifest + sha256 in the PR comment. Ran a local quick decode on a few prompts, looks okay.

bench-runner: Kicked off smoke perf run on staging-gpu-small. Command used:
```
./bench-run --model s3://redwood-models/sirocco9b/v1 --seq_len 1024 --batches 1,2,4 --iters 50 --quant none
```
I'll post the summary once finished.

sarah: Quick question on batching — do we want max_batch_tokens=4096 or 2048 for Dedicated baseline? For throughput we may push to 8192 but that affects latency on tail.

bench-runner: Early results (staging-gpu-small):
- batch=1 seq=1024: p50=145ms, p95=310ms, throughput=68 tok/s
- batch=2 seq=1024: p50=210ms, p95=420ms, throughput=130 tok/s
- batch=4 seq=1024: p50=380ms, p95=760ms, throughput=245 tok/s
Notes: memory headroom allows max_batch_tokens=6144, but latency tails grow nonlinearly past 4096. For Dedicated baseline I'd recommend max_batch_tokens=4096 with autoscale burst to 8192 if throughput spike detected.

priya: Looks good. I'll merge the PR after a quick CI pass. Also adding a tokenizer unit test for the leading-space case.

dan: FYI I validated the manifest sha against the uploaded artifact and checksum matches. No weight corruption.

maya: Awesome — once PR is merged, can we schedule a catalog readiness run and tag the model as `catalog:prelim-ready`? Also open a follow-up ticket to run 24hr stability with quantized variant.

bench-runner: Will schedule the catalog smoke this afternoon after the merge. Posting job id when queued.

maya: Thanks all :thumbsup:
